prompt: Which pair of properties is equivalent to asymmetry for every binary relation?

answers.explanation: Antisymmetry forbids two-way pairs between distinct elements; irreflexivity also forbids the diagonal case.
A loopless two-way pair has these properties but is not asymmetric.
Reflexivity creates loops, which violate asymmetry on a nonempty domain.
Equality has both properties and is not asymmetric on a nonempty domain.
Loops are allowed; equality is a counterexample.
This implies asymmetry but is stronger: an asymmetric two-step chain may lack its shortcut.
One one-way pair does not rule out a two-way pair elsewhere.
A loop may remain on one element while another element lacks its loop.
A two-way pair with no loops is antitransitive but not asymmetric.
This allows loops, and it also excludes the empty asymmetric relation.
